top_story: Trump’s threat on 12 April to blockade the Strait of Hormuz after failed Iran talks has moved from coercive signaling toward implementation, with the U.S. military on 13 April extending enforcement to all shipping in the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea east of the strait. That step sharpens a cycle set in motion weeks earlier, when Trump threatened Iran’s power grid and Tehran answered with warnings of regional escalation, making the current standoff less a discrete maritime dispute than a widening confrontation over deterrence and economic pressure. NATO allies’ refusal to join the blockade exposes Washington’s growing isolation even as the measure risks disrupting civilian commerce, energy flows, and seafarer safety across a corridor vital to Gulf livelihoods. The immediate picture is a unilateral U.S. escalation that raises the odds of miscalculation while weakening the international backing needed to sustain it.
